outputs: Generated malicious messages for injection into Message Propagation Trees to deceive rumor detection models

changes_made.explanation: Removed 'Text Summarization' and 'Other:Text Generation' as the paper does not evaluate these tasks. The paper only uses LLMs for malicious message generation as part of attack simulation. Normalized model name to standard form.
No automatic NLG evaluation metrics are used. The paper evaluates rumor detection performance using accuracy metrics, not NLG output quality.
No LLM-as-judge evaluation is conducted. LLMs are only used for generating malicious messages, not for evaluating outputs.
No human evaluation of generated outputs is mentioned in the paper.

overall_notes: This paper is primarily about defending against LLM-generated attacks on rumor detection systems, not about evaluating NLG quality. The NLG component (malicious message generation) is used as an attack vector rather than being the main focus of evaluation. The paper evaluates defense effectiveness using classification accuracy metrics, not NLG evaluation metrics.
